posts.text:
Michael Gerber nailed it in The E Myth Revisited. Most small businesses are started by a great technician who thinks knowing the work means knowing the business.

It doesn't. Doing the work and running the business are two different jobs.

This week, pick one task only you know how to do. Write the steps so someone else could.

Owners, quick one.

How fast does your business reply to a new lead right now?

A) Under 5 minutes
B) Within the hour
C) Same day
D) Whenever I get to it

Be honest. Reply with your letter and I'll tell you what it's costing you.

Building in public. My Threads went quiet for two days this week.

Not because the bot broke. Because I never built the step that writes next week's posts. The alarm went off right on time and nobody was feeding it.

Automating the posting is easy. The boring prep work is where systems actually fail.

What breaks in your business when you get busy?

Your competitor isn't better than you. They're just easier to buy from.

Clear prices. Fast replies. One click to book.

Make paying you the easiest part of their day.

Straight offer. I build an AI front desk that answers every call, texts back every missed one, and books the job while you're working.

$997 setup and $297 a month. The first 3 founding clients pay $497 setup in exchange for an honest testimonial.

DM me MONEY and I'll show you how it would work in your business.
The call you didn't answer today already called someone else.

Myth. "Word of mouth is enough."

Word of mouth brings people to your door. It doesn't answer the phone, send the quote, or follow up.

Referrals die in voicemail too.

Money move for today, 10 minutes.

1. Call your own business after hours.
2. Listen like a stranger with a leaking pipe.
3. Ask yourself if you'd wait for a callback or call the next name on Google.

Most owners never hear what their customers hear. Hear it once.

Mike Michalowicz flips the formula in Profit First. Most owners run sales minus expenses equals profit. He says sales minus profit equals expenses.

Pay yourself first, then run the business on what's left.

It forces you to cut the waste you've been ignoring. Try it with even 1% this month.

Real question for the builders.

What's the one tool you pay for that you couldn't run your business without?

Drop it below. I'll reply with how to squeeze more money out of it.

Honest build note. I built a bot that writes me a market brief every weekday before the open. Yesterday's closes, today's key levels, and today's economic calendar in one short note.

Facts only. No predictions.

The real win is that I stopped burning the first hour of my day scrolling.

What's eating your first hour?

Cheap customers cost the most.

They haggle, they complain, and they leave for $5.

Price for the customers you want to keep.

Two ways to get an AI front desk from me.

We run it. I set it up and handle the minutes, tuning, updates, and a monthly report.

You run it. One time fee. I build it in accounts you own, train your team, and hand you the keys.

Both answer every call. DM me MONEY and tell me which one you want.
Busy owners don't need more hours. They need fewer leaks.

Unpopular opinion. Most businesses don't have a marketing problem. They have a response problem.

The ads work. The leads come in. Then nobody answers for three hours.

Fix the response before you spend another dollar on ads.

Steal this prompt to win back old customers.

"Here's a list of customers who haven't booked in 6 months [paste]. Write a short, friendly text for each one that mentions their last job and gives them a reason to book again this month."

Old customers are the cheapest sale you'll ever make.

Stephen Covey's 7 Habits has one every owner needs. Begin with the end in mind.

Before you take on a client, a project, or a new tool, decide what done right looks like. Then work backward.

Most wasted money comes from starting before you knew what finished looked like.

Builders, who else is running their business with AI?

Tell me one thing you've handed to a bot. I'll go first. My bots find prospects, draft outreach, write content, watch my website, and post this.

Your turn. Let's connect.

Building in public. I built an AI that answers a business line, books appointments on a calendar, and never puts anyone on hold.

The hardest part wasn't the tech. It was making it sound like someone who actually cares.

Anyone else building with voice AI? Reply and let's trade notes.
Every business is a sales business. Some owners just haven't admitted it yet.

Free offer, no strings.

DM me MONEY and tell me your average job price. I'll show you what missed calls are probably costing you each month, using your own numbers.

If the number is small, great. If it isn't, we'll talk.
A system you trust beats a hustle you can't keep.

Friday the 13th reminder. Nothing is scarier for a small business than a phone ringing with nobody there to answer it.

Not black cats. Not ladders. Voicemail.

Prompt Friday. Copy this to write a quote that closes.

"Here's my service and price [paste]. Rewrite my quote so it opens with the customer's problem, shows what they get, explains why it's worth the price, and ends with one simple next step."

Most quotes list the work. Good quotes sell the result.

Alex Hormozi's $100M Offers has one idea worth stealing. Make an offer so good people feel stupid saying no.

That doesn't mean cheaper. It means a bigger result, less risk, faster results, and less effort for the customer.

Look at your main offer today. Which of those four can you improve?

Friday question.

What's the one task you'd pay to never do again?

Reply with it. I'll tell you if AI can take it off your plate or if you're stuck with it.

Second prompt for your Friday. This one finds slow leaks.

"Here are my last 20 customer emails and texts [paste]. Find every question customers asked more than once, then write one clear answer for each that I can put on my website."

Every repeat question is a phone call you didn't need to take.

If you have to chase payments, your process is broken, not your customers.

Clear terms. Deposit up front. Easy ways to pay.

Get paid like you mean it.

Plain offer for the weekend.

3 founding spots for my AI front desk at $497 setup, normally $997. It answers your calls, books your jobs, and texts back anyone you miss.

In return I get an honest testimonial. DM me MONEY to claim one.
Lucky businesses answer the phone.

Saturday truth. If your weekend depends on your phone staying quiet, you don't have a business yet. You have a leash.

Systems are how you take it off.

Weekend money move, 20 minutes.

1. Look at your Google Business Profile like a stranger would.
2. Check your hours, your photos, and your last 3 reviews.
3. Reply to every review you haven't answered, good or bad.

People read your replies before they ever call you.

Robert Cialdini's Influence explains reciprocity. People feel they owe you when you give first.

So give first. A free tip, a quick estimate, a useful answer.

Then make it easy for them to pay you for the rest.

Saturday question for the room.

What made you start your business?

A) Freedom
B) Money
C) Tired of having a boss
D) Saw a better way to do it

Reply with your letter. I read every one.

Building in public. My content runs on a system now. AI drafts the posts, a script publishes them on schedule, and a check fails loudly when something is missing.

It still needs me. I read every week before it goes live.

AI does the volume. Humans do the judgment.

Raise your prices on new customers first.

Your old customers never see it, and your new ones never knew the old price.

Weekend offer, straight.

If your business runs on the phone, I'll build you an AI that answers every call and books the job, even at 2 AM on a Saturday.

DM me MONEY and I'll walk you through it in 15 minutes.
Saturday night. Your phone is still ringing. Who's answering it?

Sunday truth. Revenue is vanity. Profit is sanity. Cash in the bank is reality.

Know all three numbers before Monday.

Sunday planning, 15 minutes.

1. Write down your 3 biggest money tasks for the week.
2. Put them on your calendar before anything else.
3. Ask AI to draft the emails or texts each one needs.

Monday starts with momentum instead of a pile.

James Clear writes in Atomic Habits that you don't rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.

Same in business. Your revenue goal doesn't answer the phone. Your system does.

Pick one system to tighten this week.

Sunday question.

What's one thing you'll do differently in your business this week?

Write it below. Putting it in writing makes it real.

End of week build note. I'm paper testing a trading bot right now. It doesn't touch a real dollar until it has 30 trades on the record.

Same rule for every system I build for clients. Test it where mistakes are free, then let it near the money.

What do you test before you trust it?

Money loves clarity.

Clear offer. Clear price. Clear next step.

The offer for the week ahead.

I build AI that answers your calls, books your jobs, follows up on your quotes, and asks for your reviews. I run it for you, or I build it in your accounts so you own it.

3 founding spots at $497 setup. DM me MONEY, or grab my free review kit at evogencyglobal.com/free-review-kit
New week tomorrow. Answer fast. Follow up faster.
